BATTERY REGULATION CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Which EU Batteries Regulation duties reach your battery, and by when?

Pick the battery, your role and where you are established. You get a dated timeline (label, removability, QR code, battery passport, due diligence), whether an EU operator stands behind the battery, and the duties still open.

A first read of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Dates can move with EU implementing acts. It is not legal advice.

Choose the battery, your role and where you are established, then click Check my battery.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Scope: batteries placed on the EU market, including batteries built into other products and online sales from outside the EU. Military, space and nuclear batteries are outside it.
    • 
      
  • Timeline: duties are filtered by battery category and role and ordered by the date they apply from. Duties that wait on an EU implementing act, such as the carbon-footprint declaration, show no date.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: whether your battery meets the performance, safety and durability requirements, the exact data fields of the passport, sector-law conformity, national penalties and registration fees.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
Does the EU Batteries Regulation apply to e-bikes and power banks?

    
Yes. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 covers portable batteries, light-means-of-transport batteries such as e-bike packs, starter batteries, industrial batteries and electric vehicle batteries placed on the EU market, including batteries built into other products and products sold online from outside the EU.

    
When does the battery passport apply?

    
From 18 February 2027 for light-means-of-transport batteries, industrial batteries over 2 kWh and electric vehicle batteries. A QR code on the battery links to the digital record.

    
When do the battery label and removability rules apply?

    
The general information label applies from 18 August 2026. Users must be able to remove and replace portable batteries built into appliances from 18 February 2027.

    
Do I need an authorised representative to sell batteries into the EU from outside?

    
An EU-established manufacturer, importer or authorised representative must stand behind the battery, and a seller shipping to EU buyers needs an authorised representative for producer-responsibility registration in each country it sells into.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent; a test in the code asserts there are no network calls.
